subject: Marketplace private offer — tiered commit trigger & reseller crediting
messages:
From: James Alder <james@sc-cloud.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Chopra <priya.chopra@deployer.io>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer — commit tiers and reseller crediting

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get clarification on how Redwood intends to structure the private offer for SustainCloud. Two quick items they raised:

- We need to keep our channel margin intact for the first 12 months (they typically require a line-item credit on the PO).
- The private offer must include a rollback/refund trigger in case consumption drops below commit thresholds mid-term. Procurement wants to understand the exact trigger language and the financial mechanics (pro-rata refund vs. future credit).

A couple of constraints from our side: we prefer invoices to flow to our reseller entity (CloudResell Partners) rather than Redwood billing the end customer directly — that avoids double-tax complications for our CFO. Also they asked if there’s any way to show your list price on the marketplace listing while passing a channel credit offline.

Can you share a draft of the pricing schedule and an outline of how the reseller credit waterfall would work across tiers? Happy to set a call.

Thanks,
James Alder
Director, Strategic Partnerships
SustainCloud

--

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — commit tiers and reseller crediting

Hi James — thanks, and great question. Putting Vanessa and Karthik on the thread since this touches channel ops and marketplace mechanics.

High-level answers to start:
- We can deliver a private offer with list price visible on the marketplace and an off-invoice reseller credit that preserves your partner margin. That’s a common pattern.
- For rollback/refund triggers we can support a lookback clause with a pro-rata refund (or credit) tied to consumption over a rolling 90-day window; exact wording can be tuned.

I attached a draft pricing schedule that maps commit tiers to unit prices and proposes an initial channel credit schedule (see attachment). Our suggested starting point (flexible):
- Tier A (0–$200k commit): 25% reseller credit
- Tier B ($200k–$500k): 20% reseller credit + 3% usage rebate if consumption > 110% of commit
- Tier C (>$500k): 15% reseller credit + 5% consumption rebate

Operational asks from our side: reseller needs to be set up in AWS/GCP marketplace as the purchasing entity so invoices can be routed to them; for GCP we’ll need a mapping between your reseller entity and the commitment record. Karthik — can you add marketplace constraints below?

Next steps: Vanessa will share a channel waterfall and a suggested payout window. After that I can prepare a term sheet and DocuSign envelope for approvals.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — commit tiers and reseller crediting

Thanks Rachel. James — looping in a short channel ops note and a recommended waterfall. Attachment: Channel_waterfall_v2.pdf

Key points:
- We support two execution models: pass-through credit (Redwood lists full price; we issue a direct credit to the reseller) or rebate (Redwood invoices the reseller at net after the credit). Both preserve gross margin but have different accounting impacts.
- Recommended default: pass-through credit on a line-item tied to the private offer ID. That lets the marketplace show list price while the reseller records their margin cleanly.
- Payout timing: 30–45 days after Redwood receives payment from the reseller. We can extend to 60 days for larger partners with a signed SLA.

Waterfall (example math):
- List price: $0.020/token
- Tier A credit: 25% => effective reseller take 25% of list = $0.005/token credited offline
- If commit not met after 90-day lookback: pro-rata refund equal to the unused commit at list * applicable credit %; refunds can be issued as invoice credits or future-period rebates.

Open items for legal/procurement: whether the reseller requires a separate billing relationship (we can support) and whether your CFO needs an audited invoice trace for tax reasons.

If this direction sounds good I’ll update the waterfall with line-by-line examples for your finance team.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Channel Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com

Rachel / Vanessa — appreciate the fast follow. A few clarifying points from procurement and finance:

- They are OK with a pass-through credit, but they want the effective margin at entry-level to be no lower than 28% net to the reseller. Your proposed 25% would leave them short; can Redwood flex to 28–30% for Tier A?
- On refunds: procurement prefers a future-period credit rather than cash refunds (simpler for accounting), but our legal team wants a clause that guarantees a cash pay-out if the partner dissolves mid-term.
- Billing flow: can you confirm Redwood can issue invoices directly to CloudResell Partners and set payment terms on that invoice? If not, we’ll need a short description of required steps so our systems team can map it.

I’ve quoted Vanessa’s waterfall below for reference. Happy to jump on a 30 min call if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
James

Hi all — a quick marketplace implementation note (attachment: Marketplace_matrix.md). This influences how we phrase the rollback and who is the billing party.

- AWS private offers: we can set a SellerPrivateOffer where Redwood remains the seller of record but can specify invoicing and payment instructions to route billing to a designated reseller account. That supports pass-through credits and keeps list price visible.
- GCP Marketplace: commitments are mapped to the marketplace order; we need the reseller to be configured as the purchasing entity in your partner console. GCP has fewer knobs for offline credits, so we recommend embedding credit terms in the contract and handling rebates offline.
- Azure: supports both approaches but legal requires explicit invoice flows to be documented in the private offer metadata.

Operational ask: please confirm the exact legal entity name and tax ID for CloudResell Partners so we can populate the marketplace records. Also advise whether your CFO needs an audited invoice trail vs. a simple credit memo flow.

If we get those details I’ll draft the marketplace-specific language for the rollback clause (90-day lookback + pro-rata credit) and a suggested implementation per cloud provider.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — summary and proposal below. I put the proposed term sheet in the attached doc (RDW_SustainCloud_term_sheet_v1.docx) for sign-off.

Summary of agreed mechanics (proposal):
- Entry-level Tier A: 28% reseller credit (compromise to meet SustainCloud ask).
- Tier B: 20% reseller credit + 3% consumption rebate if >110% of commit.
- Tier C: 15% reseller credit + 5% rebate.
- Payouts: 45-day reseller payout window; option to extend to 60 days with SLA scheduling.
- Rollback/refund: 90-day rolling lookback. If consumption < commit, we issue a future-period credit equal to unused commit * applicable credit %. If partner is dissolved or unable to accept credits, Redwood will issue a cash refund upon evidence of insolvency or winding down (legal to define).
- Billing flow: Redwood can invoice CloudResell Partners directly; please send full legal entity name and tax ID.

Next steps:
1) James — confirm reseller legal entity and whether procurement requires cash refunds vs credits in normal ops.
2) Vanessa/Karthik — I’ll take your waterfall and marketplace notes and bake them into the term sheet.
3) I’ll route the DocuSign link once we have legal entity details. Proposed sign-off call: Mon 07/05 10:00 AM PT (30 min).

If that sounds good I’ll get the DocuSign envelope out today.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
